transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sophie Carter (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (OrionWorks, Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Platform Eng), Maya Chen (InfoSec)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
Customer evaluating migrating inference from a mixed stack (OpenAI hosted + on-prem vLLM/TGI) to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private options. Key concerns: eval parity, latency, KV cache behavior, quantization effects, cost tradeoffs, security/KMS and SOC2 scope. Agreed to run POC benchmarking; Redwood to provide harness and pricing options.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh we'll do a quick intros then jump into what you're trying to accomplish. Aisha, do you want to kick us off with a little bit of context?
[00:09] Aisha: yeah sure. So, um OrionWorks we've been running customer-facing chat and document QA features. Right now it's a mix - we use OpenAI for a lot of high-quality generation, and we also have an on-prem inference fleet using vLLM/T-G-I stacks for lower cost, low latency in region stuff. The problem is parity and ops complexity, like two different runtime behaviours, uh and the teams want one place to run that gives consistent perf and ties to security controls.
[00:36] Marco: so you're running both OpenAI and a self-hosted vLLM/TGI? and are you doing quantization on the on-prem side?
[00:43] Tom: yeah, we quantize to 4-bit for most seq lengths; we use quantization for cost, but sometimes output quality degrades for few-shot prompts. Also kv cache management is custom - we have sticky sessions to keep cache warm for active users.
[00:58] Sophie: right, and what's the main driver for moving? Is it cost, reliability, compliance, or all of the above?
[01:05] Aisha: all of the above, but order of priority is: parity with OpenAI outputs for our customer-facing flows, then latency SLAs for live chat, and then cost predictability. Compliance is non-negotiable for some customers, so VPC or private deployment is on the table.
[01:21] Maya: from a security standpoint we need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs retained 13 months, and we're scoped for SOC2 in Q1. We also need to see encryption-in-transit details and SAML SSO for the console.
[01:33] Sophie: that's helpful. Redwood has three modes: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For compliance we typically recommend Dedicated or Private. For the parity requirement you mentioned, we usually run eval parity tests which compare outputs and flag regressions. Can you describe the parity tests you run today?
[01:50] Aisha: we use a set of ~1200 prompts across intents, and we do automated similarity and human review on a subset. Our biggest worry is that when you switch kernels or quantize differently, the tokens change or there's higher hallucination, which then increases human review cost.
[02:07] Marco: yeah, quantization and kernel selection can change logits slightly; we can run the same prompt set and produce diff stats and confusion matrices. One question — are you using function-calls heavily or structured outputs?
[02:19] Tom: mostly structured JSON outputs for the QA system, yes function-calls for a subset, and streaming for chat.
[02:26] Sophie: perfect, that's useful. For streaming we support chunked responses and function-call semantics; for structured outputs we can pin sampler/temperature and provide reproducible seeds for evals.
[02:36] Aisha: how do you handle prefix/KV cache in Redwood? The vLLM stack we run has a pretty aggressive KV strategy that keeps prompts in memory per user session. If you move to hosted, will that kill our latency?
[02:48] Marco: good question. Our runtime supports automatic KV caching and also request-level sticky routing in Dedicated. In Hosted, we have a mix of caching layers — prefix cache and per-model KV cache — and we can align policies to mimic vLLM behavior. There are some latency tradeoffs if you can't have long-lived GPU-resident caches; Dedicated gives more control.
[03:05] Maya: is there a way to have customer-managed KMS in Hosted? we need KMS keys we control.
[03:10] Sophie: yes, for Private deployments you manage keys; for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS for disk and secret encryption; Hosted can support envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key in many cases, but we'll need to review specifics in the SOC doc. I'll attach the KMS section.
[03:23] Aisha: what's the typical performance delta between your Dedicated cluster and our vLLM current numbers? we see p99 latencies around 120ms for short prompts on our infra.
[03:32] Marco: depends on model and sequence length; for similar GPU type and quant profiles we typically match or beat VLLM for steady-state throughput due to our kernel selection and continuous batching. For cold-cache p99 we can be higher unless KV warm is available. We can run a direct benchmark.
[03:46] Tom: ok good. Another thing — we're on a custom TGI variant with some plugin ops. How much model-ops work is needed to onboard?
[03:54] Marco: usually we can onboard TGI models with minor adaptation; sometimes tokenizers or custom ops need small patches. We keep a compatibility map and we'll do a test run. If it's within common ops, we won't need deep changes.
[04:06] Sophie: timeline — do you have a hard date where you need to pick a path?
[04:09] Aisha: we'd like to run a POC before end of Q1; ideally kickoff in early Jan, have a 2–4 week POC with performance and parity checks, and then decide on Dedicated vs Private by mid-Feb.
[04:21] Sophie: that's doable. Proposal: two POC tracks — Hosted quick path (fast to start, lower friction) and Dedicated/Private track for parity and compliance. We'll scope both, you can pick which to run first.
[04:33] Maya: for procurement we will need standardized SOW and security questionnaire answered. Any enterprise paperwork ahead of POC?
[04:40] Sophie: we'll send a POC SOW and our security pack (SOC2, ISO references) and a short vendor questionnaire response. We'll also include sample SLAs for Dedicated.
[04:50] Marco: for the benchmark we'll want your target prompts, a representative batch distribution, and an example of your current vLLM config (quantization, batch sizes, tokenization). We'll run both throughput and quality evals and provide a parity report.
[05:02] Tom: can you share the harness? we'd rather run the baseline on our infra too.
[05:06] Marco: yes, we'll provide the harness; ideally we run Redwood-hosted baseline and you run the harness in your environment to compare apples-to-apples. We'll also instrument logs and trace tokens to help debug differences.
[05:17] Aisha: and pricing — what's the rough delta on cost for Dedicated POC vs Hosted?
[05:22] Sophie: quick ballpark: Hosted is usage-based, so POC can be lower entry; Dedicated has a small reserved footprint cost but predictable throughput which helps unit economics for high-volume. I'll include concrete numbers in the pricing sheet.
[05:34] Maya: one more security - we need attenuation on logs, redaction patterns for PII before logs leave our VPC. Is that something supported?
[05:41] Marco: yes, we support configurable redaction hooks and pre-send filtering in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we have redaction rules but for regulated PII-heavy workloads we recommend Private so nothing leaves your control plane.
[05:55] Sophie: ok, looks like we have clear next steps. I'll send the SOW and security pack. Marco will drop the harness and run an initial run by Monday, 12/22. Maya will share the compliance contacts. Aisha will provide the prompt set.
[06:10] Aisha: great, thanks. Anything else?
[06:13] Tom: no, that's it from infra.
[06:15] Sophie: awesome. I'll follow up in email with links and proposed kickoff times. thanks everyone.

End of call.

Notes/attachments referenced (not attached): POC_SOW_template.pdf, redwood-security-pack-2025.pdf, benchmark-harness-v1.zip, sample-configs/tgi-to-redwood.md
